Sikder Mahmudur Razi, Advocate with Md Omar Faruk, Advocates—For the Petitioner.

Md Obaidur Rahman, Advocate—For the Opposite party No. 2.

Md Fazlur Rahman Khan, DAG with Md Shafiquel Islam Siddique DAG with Md Jahir Ahmed, AAG and Md Shafiquzzaman, AAG—For the State-opposite party No. 1.
parties:
Abdur Razzak Mozumder --------- Convicted-petitioner
vs
State and another -------- Opposite parties
full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim, J: In the present application filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, a Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 11-7-2019 passed by the Metropolitan Joint Sessions Judge, Court No. 4, Chattogram in Sessions Case No. 3653 of 2019 arising out of CR Case No. 1283 of 2017 convicting the petitioner under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 and sentencing him to suffer simple imprisonment for 1 (one) year with a fine of Taka 3,62,80,000 should not be quashed and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Facts, in brief, are that the opposite party No. 2 filed a petition of complaint on 03-12-2017 being CR Case No. 1283 of 2017 before the Metropolitan Magistrate Court No. 4, Chattogram under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (In short, the Act) against the convict-petitioner alleging, inter alia, that there was a business relation between the accused and complainant. In connection to that relation the complainant entitled to get Taka 3,62,80,000. To pay the said money the accused issued the case cheque dated 30-7-2017 maintained by his business concern named M/s PPP Enterprise with the National Credit and Commerce Bank Limited, Cumilla Branch. The complainant presented the said cheque for encashment to Brac Bank Limited, Sk. Mujib Road Branch, Chittagong on 20-9-2017, but the bank dishonoured the same with the comment 'Account Closed/dormant/ Blocked'. Under the circumstances, the complaint sent a legal notice to the petitioner on 17-10-2017 through registered post, but it was returned on 23-10-2017 with the remarks "বর্তমানে উল্লেখিত হোল্ডিং নাম্বারে এবং বিল্ডিং এই নামে প্রাপক নাই।" 

 3. On receipt of the petition of complaint, the learned Magistrate concern upon examining the complainant under section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure took cognizance of the offence against the accused-petitioner under section 138 of the Act on 3-12-2017 and issued summons upon him for appearance. Thereafter, on 7-1-2018 the learned Magistrate issued Warrant of Arrest against the accused since the summons was returned. Warrant of Arrest has been returned on 22-4-2018, the learned Magistrate issued Warrant of Proclamation and Attachment against the accused. Thereafter, receiving the report of W&P/A on 3-3-2019, the learned Magistrate passed an order of paper publication and, finally, on 11-4-2019 made the case ready for initiation of trial in absentia and, accordingly, the learned Magistrate send the record before the learned Trial Court. Thereafter, on receiving the record the learned Court of Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chattogram renumbered the case as Sessions Case No. 3653 of 2019. Subsequently, on 23-6-2019 the learned Trial Court framed Charge against the accused under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. On 4-7-2019 the complainant as PW-1 was testified before the learned Trial Court and exhibited cheques along with relevant documents to prove the prosecution case. Since the accused was not present during trial the examination under section 342 could not possible and, accordingly, the learned trial court on 9-7-2019 heard the argument of the state and, finally, on 11-7-2019 the learned Trial Court pronounced the judgment and Order of Conviction and Sentence dated 11-7-2019 in Sessions Case No. 3653 of 2019 arising out of CR Case No. 1283 of 2017 convicting the accused-petitioner under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, and, further, sentencing him to suffer simple imprisonment for 1 (one) year and to pay of Taka 3,62,80,000 (Taka Three Crore Sixty Two Lac Eighty Thousand) only. 

 4. Thereafter, the convict-petitioner was arrested from Cumilla on 17-9-2019 long after passing of his conviction and first time came to know about the present case. Then the convict-petitioner filed Criminal Revision Case No. 3394 of 2019 under section 435 read with section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained bail for a period of 2 (two) months and was further directed to file an appeal by depositing 50% of the dishonored cheque amount but he failed to comply with the said direction, accordingly Rule was discharged as infructuous on 12-3-2020. That it is stated that during pendency of the said Criminal Revision, convict-petitioner filed the instant Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7731 of 2020 on 05-2-2020 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained present Rule and bail on 13-2-2020. 

 5. Present Rule was contested by the opposite party No. 2 by filing counter-affidavit dated 2-11-2020 and supplementary-counter-affidavit dated 10-11-2020. In those Affidavits opposite party No. 2 clearly stated that after passing of the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 11-7-2019, the convict-petitioner earlier filed Criminal Revision No. 3394 of 2019 under section 435 read with section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 before this Hon'ble Court impugning the Order dated 21-11-2019 passed by the learned Metropolitan Joint Sessions Judge, Fourth Court, Chittagong in Sessions Case No. 3653 of 2019 rejecting the prayer for bail till filling of Appeal against the Judgment and Order of Conviction and Sentence dated 11-7-2019 passed in Sessions Case No. 3653 of 2019 arising out of CR Case No. 1283 of 2017 convicting the petitioner under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, and sentencing him to suffer simple imprisonment for 01 (one) year and to pay of Taka 3,62,80,000 (Taka Three Crore Sixty Two Lac Eighty Thousand); that upon hearing the Criminal Revisional Application, a Single Bench of the Hon'ble High Court Division by Order dated 8-12-2019 issued a Rule upon the opposite parties and further passed an ad-interim order enlarging the convict-petitioner on bail for a period of 2 (two) months from date subject to depositing the passport of the convict-petitioner being No. BJ 068481 before the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chattogram and the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chattogram is directed to accept the bail bond after receiving the said passport of the convict-petitioner and keeping the same in the custody of the Court. The convict-petitioner is at liberty to withdraw his passport after filing the appeal in this Court by depositing 50% of the Cheque amount through Chalan in the trial court, failing which, the order of bail shall stand canceled and the Rule will be discharged and also directed the convict-petitioner to file an Affidavit-of-Compliance on or before 10th February, 2020 which was not complied by the petitioner which proves that the petitioner do not obey the order passed by the Hon'ble Court; that since the convict-petitioner failed to comply with the order and remained absent at the time of hearing of the Rule, same was discharged with cost of Taka 10,000 by order dated 12-3-2020; that it is further stated that the question of receiving or serving notice issued under section 138(1)(b) of the Negotiable Instruments Act upon the drawer are questions of fact to be decided by trial court and that since the petitioner did not come with clean hands, and that an alternative forum is available under section 138A and the convict petitioner had waived his right to prefer an appeal, subject to fulfillment of the condition laid down in section 138A and, as such, present application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not maintainable. 

 6. The learned Advocate Mr Sikder Mahmudur Razi, for the convict-petitioner at the outset emphatically submits that the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence has been secured by committing fraud and same also suffers from malafideness and therefore the entire proceeding in an abuse of the process of the court. He further submits that mandatory provision of Negotiable Instruments Act and Code of Criminal Procedure has been violated in every stage in the instant case. Moreover, the process of summons, warrant of arrest and W/P and A were not served and executed in due course of law and the complaint-opposite-party No. 2 instead of publishing notice in wide circulated National dailies, published the same in two Local dailies of District Chattogram which have no wide circulation. Hence the conviction and sentence passed against the convict-petitioners is liable to be quashed for securing ends of justice. In support of his submissions learned Advocate has referred the decisions reported in 49 DLR 520, 6 BLC 184, 2012 BLD 570, 21 BLT 112 and AIR 2012 (SC) 700 and 15 BLT (AD) 267. 

 7. Mr Obaidur Rahman, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the complaint-opposite-party No. 2 vehemently submits that there is no scope for the convict-petitioner to file an application under section 561A without following the mandatory provision laid down under section 138A of the Negotiable Instruments Act where there remains specific alternative remedy prescribed under section 138A of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 to file appeal against the judgment and order of conviction and sentences passed by the Sessions Judge subject to deposit of 50% of the dishonoured cheque amount before filling the appeal. He further submits that when there is specific provisions in Negotiable Instruments Act for filing appeal with a pre-condition associated to deposit 50% of the dishonoured cheque amount, the present petition under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not maintainable. He lastly submits that the convict-petitioner filed the case under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure only to delay and defeat the realisation of Taka 3,62,80,000 by the opposite-party No. 2. As such the petitioner has not come with clean hands and is not entitled to invoke jurisdiction under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Accordingly learned Advocate prayed for discharge of the Rule with cost. 

 10. We have gone through the Judgment, oral evidence of PW's and the documents exhibited in the case. The learned Sessions Judge after considering the evidence of 3 PW's and materials on record rightly found that the drawer has failed to pay the amount shown in cheque (Exhibit-2) within the stipulated period on receipt of legal notice issued under clause (b) of the section 138(1) of the Negotiable Instruments Act and the complainant filed the complaint petition within the time prescribed as provided under section 141(b) of Negotiable Instruments Act. Thus it is evident that the trial court after consideration of the legal aspect and appreciating the oral and documentary evidence on record rightly found that the petitioner committed offence under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act and accordingly convicted accused-petitioner and imposed fine of Taka 3,62,80,000. 

 15. Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is intended to secure the ends of justice or to prevent the abuse of the process of the court. But, in the instant case, this application filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure amounts to clear abuse of the process of this Division. Hence, necessary order should be passed accordingly. 

 19. The submission made by the learned Advocate for the convict-petitioner that the notice was not served under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, which is essentially a question of fact, to be proved by adducing evidence at the time of trial, in as much as there is specific assertion in the petition of complaint that such a notice was, in fact, served. Hence this fact cannot be decided by this court exercising jurisdiction under section 561A of the Code. The principle of law in this regard has been set as rest by our Appellate Division in the case of Nizamuddin Mahmood vs Abdul Hamid Bhuyian, reported in 60 DLR (AD) 165. 

 20. Upon perusal of the provision section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (as amended on 9-2-2006) there appears that no intention on the part of the legislatures to give any benefit of doubt to an individual accused in a case under section 138 of the Act, rather, intention of the legislators appears to be to secure beneficial interest of the drawee of a cheque, as is apparent from a mere perusal of this section. This intention of the legislators has been made further clear by incorporating section 138A of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 prescribing provision for depositing not less than 50% of the amount of the dishonoured cheque is a pre-requisite for filing appeal against any order or sentence under section 138(1) of the Act. 

 21. Accordingly, we hold that this petition under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not maintainable. We further hold that this court cannot pass any order or judgment, in exercise power vested under section 561A, or under any other section, that would have effect of rendering provisions of law a total nullity or that shall come into conflict within specific provision of any law, in this case with the provisions of section 138A of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. 

 22. In view of the discussions made above and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, provision of section 138A of the Negotiable Instruments Act, and the decisions of our Apex Court reported in 28 DLR (AD) 28, 31 DLR (AD) 69, we do not find any merit in this Rule. 

 24. The conviction and sentence dated 11-7-2019 passed by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Court No- 4, Chattogram in Sessions Case No. 3653 of 2019 arising out of CR Case No. 1283 of 2017 convicting the convict-petitioner under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act is hereby affirmed.
